blocks.x: What Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning looks like when it has to survive an audit: scoped deliverables, weekly evidence, named control owners and a committed delta per gate.

Batch thinking caps business performance: fraud caught after settlement, stockouts discovered at replenishment, churn addressed after the customer calls to leave. We build streaming backbones — Kafka or managed equivalents, Flink/Spark Structured Streaming processing, exactly-once semantics where money moves — feeding online feature stores and decision APIs that act within the customer moment, the machine cycle or the fraud window.

Engineering discipline makes it trustworthy: schema-first topics, watermark handling for late events, back-pressure design, and chaos drills that prove recovery. We pair the stack with event-storming workshops so the topics and events reflect how the business actually works — the difference between a streaming platform and a streaming mess.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
